literal: Return expecting-not duty; towards rain what will-do indeed world?
translation: True duty expects no return. What can the world ever do in return for the rain?
modern: கைம்மாறு எதிர்பார்க்காமல் உதவுவதே சிறந்த கடமையாகும். மழைக்கு இந்த உலகம் கைம்மாறாக என்ன செய்துவிட முடியும்?
explanation: This couplet defines true benevolence as a duty that expects nothing in return. The word 'kaṭappāṭu' signifies a moral obligation to help others selflessly. The poet compares this unconditional giving to the rain, which sustains life without asking for anything back. By asking what the world could possibly give back to the rain, the couplet emphasizes that the highest form of giving is entirely one-sided.
